note.text: Explain and question a proposal instead of accepting it because the speaker sounds confident. Separate knowledge, prediction and questions still needing answers. Ask about relevant skills, resources and demand. Cost differs from income, and predicted income does not prove profit. This fictional language exercise supplies no real business recommendation or return. It prepares written discussion notes; turn-taking and delivery require a partner or teacher.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections

paper_task.prompt: Prepare a discussion comparing the fictional proposals. Give reasons, ask about skills, resources and demand, and state what remains unknown. Practise responding with a partner if possible.
model: Bih proposes illustrated club bookmarks; Ayuk proposes supervised document-layout help. Bih can show drawings, while Ayuk has practised arranging text. Neither proposal has been tried with interested customers.

I would ask what skill each proposer can demonstrate, what materials or access are needed and how demand would be checked. A popular idea may require resources the group lacks. I would consider an authorised trial after those questions are answered; these notes do not establish that either proposal will make a profit.
checklist: Demonstrated skill: an ability supported by a relevant example.
Resource question: a request identifying what an activity requires.
Demand uncertainty: recognition that customer interest remains untested.
Cautious conclusion: a judgement matching the available evidence.
Use relevant original details and check sentence boundaries, agreement and spelling.
